content: This being New Year's day, and also the anniversary of my assuming the Government of this Colony three years ago, I ordered it to be observed as a Holiday throughout the Territory, and that the Troops & Government Artificers and Labourers should receive the usual Donations of Spirits and Fresh Meat. — I received at Noon the Congratulations of the Principal Civil and Military Inhabitants of the Colony; and Congratulatory Addresses were presented to me from the Inhabitants of Sydney, Windsor, Parramatta, and Liverpool! — I entertained the Civil & Military Officers of Government with their Families, the Officers of H.M. Ship _Samarang_, and other Strangers now at Sydney & the Gentlemen who were deputed to present the Addresses at Dinner today; 48 Persons having sat down at Table! —

The _Spring Grove_, South Sea Whaler, Capt. Douglas, anchored this afternoon in the cove from England, which she left on the 17th. of July last. — A Letter recd. by this conveyance by Mrs. M. from her Sister Margaret mentions my Broyr. Charles having married a young Lady of Fortune at Edinburgh in June last; – but no letters have been recd. from himself. — I have recd. no Public Dispatches – and very few Private Letters, but have had the pleasure to hear that all our Friends at Home were well at the departure of the this Ship. — Capt. Jno. Maclaine has succeeded to the Majority of the 73d. _vice_ Cleaveland deceased. —
Kept as usual Ball & Supper – 115 Persons entertained at Supr.

Returned this day to Sydney from Parramatta whither I had gone on Saturday the 30th. Ulto., and spent my Birth-Day anniversary there on Sunday the 31st. January; Col: & Mrs. & Miss Davey, Dr. & Mrs. Redfern Capt. Locker 8th Lt. Dns, Major Jno. Maclaine, Capt. Kenny, Lt. Raymond, and our own Family (– in all 14 –) being the Party.

This morning early between 1 and 2,O'Clock Lt. Jno. Maclaine, A,D.C. being on board the Ship _Eugenia_Capt. Blayd, in a state of extreme intoxication went up aloft in order to get to the Mizzen Top-mast Head, a stay by which he held having given way he fell down on the Deck from a height of 35 Feet, and dislocated his left arm in a most shocking and dangerous manner. The bone was set by Dr. Redfern between 2 & 3 OClock, and Mr. M. was brought on shore in a Cott [sic] to the Govt. House about 11,OClock, where now lies dangerously ill: – such being the Consequence of low Drinking and intemperance, this unfortunate young man deserves little pity!

Went on a Visit to Parramatta this morning before Breakfast to examine the New Store & other Public Works, and returned to Sydney to Dinner in the Evening. — The Ship _Eugenia_ Capt. Blayd sailed early this morning for Batavia. — Capt. Locker 8th Lt. Dnsand Lt. Aston Madras Horse Artillery went Passengers in her. — I wrote several Letters to Friends in India Pr. this Ship as Pr. List kept thereof. —
Went to and spent this day at Parramatta to look at the Works carrying on there; and returned to Sydney on Wedy. morning the 3d. of March! —

The first Public Fair ever held in this Territory, by regular authority, was held this day at Parramatta at the Public Market Place for the Sale of Horses, Horned Cattle & Sheep, and was numerously attended, with a great Show of Cattle. — I went up to Parramatta on Wednesday and returned again to Sydney on Friday morning.
Went up this day from Sydney to Parramatta. —
Went to Windsor — Travelling by the old Road through the Seven Hills and by the South Creek, which we crossed at Mr. Lange's & Mr. Rouse's Farms – where a Water Mill might be safely erected. —
Rested at Windsor – and examined the New Bridge erecting over the South Creek.

Set out early in the morning for Emu Island. — Breakfasted at Capt. Woodriffe's Farm on the Nepean – which we afterwards crossed in a Boat – sending on our Horses across by the Ford a little below where we Breakfasted. — Travelled on Horseback all over Emu Island – which runs about three miles along the River from North to South, and about Two miles in, West, towards the mountains. — This is a fine Tract of Land well watered – and capable of grazing between 4 and 500 Head of Horned Cattle all the Year through.

Returned home in the afternoon by Castlereagh at which Township we Stopt [sic] for half an Hour to examine the Grounds and Scite [sic] intended for erecting the Parsonage House upon – a very beautiful Spot. — Our Party on this Excursion besides Mrs. M. and myself were Revd. Mr. Marsden, Mr. Cox, Mr. Geo. Palmer, Mr. Fitzgerald, and Major Maclaine & Capt. Antill. —
Rested at Windsor, being Good Friday.

Set out early this morning accompanied by the same Party as above, with the exception of Messrs. Palmer & Fitzgerald and addition of Lieut. Maclaine, on an Excursion to Grosse's [sic] Head. — Breakfasted at the confluence of the Grose & Nepean Rivers; crossed the latter on Horseback by an easy Ford close to our Breakfast Place, and ascended the mountain to the Summit, which we reached about Noon – the distance thither from where we crossed the Nepean being about Five miles. — From the Summit of Grose's Head we had a most picturesque grand and extensive prospect in every direction; being here about 600 Feet above the level of the Grosse [sic] River in a perpendicular direction. — The windings of the river below us appeared beautiful – with one very fine Straight Reach a quarter of a mile long. —

Returned Home in the afternoon by Richmond at which township we halted to look at the New School House, now nearly finished, and which is to be used as a temporary chapel till a proper Church is built for this District.
Rested & went to Church at Windsor.
Returned to Parramatta.
Rested at Parramatta – visited the Store & other works going on there. —
Returned to Sydney to Breakfast. —

Mrs. M. was taken very ill this morning – and continued so till Wedy. 5th. May, when she had a miscarriage; being the Sixth she has had at Home & in this Country since the Birth of our darling little Baby!!!
Mrs. M.'s complaint ceased this day and her health begins to improve. —

I this day Inspected the 73d. Regt., and had the Officers to dine with me at the Govt. House afterwards. It rained almost all day, and of course the weather was very unfavorable for our Review.

N.B. No Ladies dined with us on this day. —
Had two large Norfolk Pine Trees, presented to Mrs. M. by S. Lord Esqr., removed from that Gentleman's Garden, and planted at the Gate opposite to Macquarie Street. —

Had another large Norfolk Pine Tree, removed from the same Gentleman's Garden at Dobride (5½ miles from Sydney) to the lower Field in Govt. Domain, where it was this morning Planted with a large Ball of its own Native Earth. — This Tree is about feet high. [number omitted]

Set out at Noon this day for Parramatta (accompanied by Mrs. M. Mrs. Cowper & her Child) on an Excursion to the interior, including Windsor and all the Grazing Grounds & Stock-Yards at present occupied by the Govt. Cattle.

On **Wedy. [19th. May]**
I visited the Stock Yards Nos. 1, 2, 3 & 4, in old Cow Pastures, riding 48 miles this day.

On **Thursday [20th. May]**
Set out for Windsor, visiting on my way thither the Govt. Stock-Yards on the East Creek & Rooty Hill. —

On **Friday 21st. May —**
Visited Wilberforce and marked out the Scite [sic] of the new intended School-House in that Township. —

On **Saturday 22d.**
Visited Richmond School House.

On **Monday 24th.**
Returned to Parramatta Visiting the Govt. Stock & Yard at Seven Hills on my way.

On **Tuesdy. 25th.**
Went to Town of Liverpool, marked out the Scite [sic] of a New Store & Granary there and dined wt. Mr. Moore J.P. at his new House.

On **Friday 28th. May —**
Returned to Sydney at Noon, no Vessels having arrived there during my absence! L.M.

This auspicious Day – the anniversary of our beloved Monarch's Birth – was observed as a Holiday throughout the Territory – and celebrated with the usual demonstrations of Joy. — I entertained the Gentlemen of the Colony at Dinner, consisting of 74 Persons, and the Ladies at Supper – at which 120 Persons sat down. — The Company did not break up till 1,O'Clock the following morning.

The Transport Ship _Fortune_ wt. 196 male Convicts anchored this day in the Harbour from England from whence she sailed on the 13th. of Decr. last. — Deputy Comy. Genl. David Allan & Family; Mr. Hogan Dy. Asst. Comy. Genl., and Messrs. Brodie & Hobson Clerks in Commissariat Department came Passengers in this Ship; together wt. Ensn. Dawson & a Detachment of 30 soldiers of the 73d. Regt. as a Guard for said Ship.

The Ship _Minstrel_ Capt. Reed sailed this day for England, having Major Maclaine & Lt. Leyne of 73d. Regt. on board as Passengers. —

I sent my Dispatches for England Pr. Major Maclaine – as per Receipt of do. —
I set out this day on an Excursion to Parramatta & Windsor, accompanied by Mrs. M. & Family; and also by Mr. & Mrs. Allan. —
We returned to Sydney at 1. P.M. this day after a pleasant Excursion!

From present appearances, and from her being quite well and free from her usual monthly Complaint since the 25th. of last month, now 30 Days, there is some reason to hope that my dearest Elizabeth is pregnant, and that she has now been so for three weeks past! — She is at present in very good health – and may the Almighty Ruler of all events grant that our mutual fervent prayers and most earnest wishes to have offspring may at length be realized – and thereby complete our Earthly happiness! —
I took a ride in the Carriage to Parramatta this morning after Breakfast to view the Improvements carrying on there – and returned to Sydney again by 3,OClock. —
Visited Parramatta again this day after Breakfast & returned to Sydney by 3. P.M. —

I took a ride in the Carriage to Parramatta accompanied by Capt. Antill & Mr. Meehan to see the Works & Improvements carrying on there – and to see a new Road marked out from Parramatta to Kissing Point; returning Home to Dinner. —
I visited Parramatta to view the Improvements carrying on there this forenoon in the Carriage accompanied by Capt. Antill, and retured again to Sydney before 3,O'Clock. —

I went to Parramatta to lay the Foundation Stone of the Building intended for the reception of the Female Orphans – who are to be removed from Sydney to Parramatta as soon as this new Building is finished. — I returned to Town to Dinner. —

I went up to Windsor to view the Improvements going on there, accompanied by Capt. Antill and Mr. Meehan in the Carriage, Breakfasting at Parramatta. — I staid one night at Windsor, and returned to Sydney at 1. OClock P.M. on Wednesday the 29th. Septr. having Breakfasted at Parramatta – and rested there for two hours. —
The second Parramatta Fair was held this day – and I went up early this morning in my Carriage accompanied by Secry. Campbell and Brigade Major Antill to see it, returning to Sydney to Dinner.

This forenoon _The Earl Spencer_ Convict Transport Ship commanded by Capt. Wm. Mitchell anchored in the Harbour from England, from whence she sailed on the 2d. of June last, touching only at Madeira which she left 2d. of July. — She brings 196 male Convicts – wt. a Guard of one Subn. (Ensign Bicknell) & 38 men of the 73d., together wt. several Free Settlers, and one asst. Surgeon (Mr. Young) for the Colony. I have received Public Dispatches by the Earl Spencer, and also a great many Private Letters from my Friends at home, all of which contain good news. By this conveyance I am informed, tho' not officially, of the certainty of my being appointed a Major General in a large Brevet made by the Prince Regent on the 4th. of June last. —

I have also received a full and particular account from my dear Brother Charles of his being happily united in marriage to Miss Marrianne [sic] Willison, a highly accomplished young Lady, wt. a Fortune of £12000. — This happy event took place on [date omitted in text: 15 June 1812]

I have likewise heard of my Nephew Hugh having succeeded to a Majority in the 77th. lately without Purchase – and that he is likely to be still fit for Service.

Accounts have been received by this oppy. of Murdh. Lochbuy's being married to a Daughter of Dond. Mc.Laine Drimnins, and of Flora Lochbuy being married to Dr. Allan Maclain in Mull !!! —

My dear Mrs. Macquarie received the mournful accounts of the Death of her good old Aunt Mrs. Campbell of Corwhin, in Wigmore Street London; but which event might naturally have been looked for from her advanced age! —

I went up in the Carriage this forenoon to Parramatta, accompanied by Capt. Antill & Mr. Meehan, to view the works carrying on there and mark out some new Streets; which having done, we returned to Sydney to Dinner! —
I reviewed the 73d. Regt. this morning (for the first time) dressed in my Full Uniform as Brigadier General. — I entertained the Officers & a number of other Gentlemen at Dinner! — L.M.

This being the anniversary of my marriage with my dearest Elizabeth – six Years ago – we had a small Party of Friends to dine with us to celebrate the auspicious day, consisting of Mr. & Mrs. Riley, Mr. & Mrs. Redfern, Dr. Wentworth, Dr. Mileham, Major Cameron – and our own Family. — Our happiness is greatly increased in keeping this Day by the gratifying reflection that my dear Elizabeth is now certainly Pregnant and God grant her Pregnancy may come to maturity – & prove fortunate! —

I set out in my own Carriage from Sydney at ¼ before 6 this morning accompanied by Capt. Antill & Capt. Wm. Mitchell of the Earl Spencer on an Excursion to Windsor, principally for the purpose of opening the New Bridge over the South Creek at the place; — which ceremony took place accordingly at ½ past 1. P.M. this day; – the Magistrates of Windsor and the Contractors for the Bridge having met me there at that hour, when I crossed the Bridge in my Carriage. — Besides the Magistrates, Secry. Campbell, Capt. Glenholme, and Lieut. Bell of the Madras N. Infy. were present at this Ceremony; these three Gentlemen having accompanied me from Parramatta, where we stopt [sic] to Breakfast. In the afternoon I took a ride on Horseback wt. Capt. Mitchell along the Banks of the Hawky. as far as a mile below Blighton and was much gratified to see so very good an appearance of a Crop. —

Rode wt. Capt. Mitchell &c. &c. along the Banks of the Hawky. as far as the confluence of the Nepean & Grose Rivers; and was equally gratified wt. the fine appearance of the Crops in that part of the Country.
I returned to Sydney at ½ past 1. P.M.

I took a ride in the Carriage early this morning to Parramatta to view the works & Improvements now carrying on there. — Took a ride after Breakfast accompanied by Mr. Marsden Mr. Oxley Capt. Mitchell & Capt. Antill to Prospect & Toongabbee Districts – and afterwards to the new Female Orphan School House now building at Parramatta. —

Returned in the Evening to Sydney to Dinner, accompanied by Capt.. Antill & Mitchell!

My dearest Elizabeth has this day completed the Sixth month of her Pregnancy – and is – thank God! in very good health & doing very well!

N.B. Mrs. M. felt the Child, She is now Pregnant of, quicken for the first time on Thursday the 21st. of Octr. last – and it has ever since continued very lively!!!

I went up in the Carriage early this morning to Parramatta to see the works &c. there accompanied by Dr. Redfern – and returned to Sydney between 1 and 2,O'Clock. — N.B. I visited the Genl. Hospl. at Parramatta!!! —
